causalModel.founding: The Teeth of Sithis is the largest Sithis temple in Murkmire. The Clutch of Nisswo tends the temple. The temple no longer serves its original purpose.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: The temple stands at the end of a pilgrim route. It stands on the fringe marsh by the coast, 35 m from the open sea. Six black stone teeth stand in the shallows there. The temple was built to frame them.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: The Clutch maintain the temple precisely. They preach that the loss of its purpose is itself the teaching.
causalModel.pressures: The temple's original purpose is lost. At least one faction claims to have found the purpose out.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: A rediscovery of the temple's function would split the Clutch.

districts.notes: The sacred ground of the Clutch of Nisswo: the bank above the colonnade and the two scaffold doors into the temple.

why.what: The district is the tended ground of the largest Sithis temple in Murkmire. The Clutch of Nisswo keep the ground.
why.whyHere: The temple was built to frame the teeth. The teeth stand at the end of the pilgrims' track down the coast.
why.whyNeighbours: Five other places lie within 200 m of the temple, at 91 to 182 m away. Of the tracks nearby, the pilgrim track from Lilmoth alone ends at the temple. Lilmoth lies about 410 m away.
why.playerPurpose: The district is the end of a pilgrimage. The Clutch hold their rite here. Two ways lead down into the temple's drowned rooms.
why.microGeography: The bank falls south-west at about ten degrees to brown sea water. The top of the bank stands 5 m above the tide.

parcels.groundFitWhy: The door is set into the hillside: the bank stands against the back of its portico, so the ground climbs from the sill to the hill under its footprint and the sill sits at the lowest ground.
parcels.orientationWhy: The west scaffold turns its door east. The door faces the track that the pilgrims come down.

why.what: The parcel holds the Clutch's west scrubbing scaffold. The scaffold stands over the first door down into the temple.
why.whyHere: King of the Murkmire set the temple's first door here. The Clutch's frame stands over that door.
why.whySpot: The parcel lies west of the track's last stretch. It stands on firm bank, so the frame needs no stilts in water.
why.whyNeighbours: The west scaffold answers the east scaffold across the track. A pilgrim passes between the two scaffolds.
why.playerPurpose: The parcel holds the first way into the lower temple. The temple's loop to the east door begins here.
why.microGeography: The parcel stands on the upper bank, 3 m above the water. The ground falls gently toward the sea.

playerPurpose.note: The first way down into the temple: a scaffold door that opens onto the stair.
The pilgrims land, the rite is held on the colonnade and the scrubbing is checked here, so every stage of the Teeth quest is staged at this stair.

why.what: The parcel holds the Clutch's east scrubbing scaffold. The scaffold stands over the second door into the temple.
why.whyHere: The temple's second door is here in the plugin. The band of the Clutch keep this door.
why.whySpot: The east scaffold stands east of the track. It stands on the bank's shoulder, where the band can see the whole colonnade.
why.whyNeighbours: The east scaffold answers the west scaffold across the track. The way runs to the water between the two scaffolds.
why.playerPurpose: The parcel holds the second way into the temple. The band sleeps here. The temple's loop comes out here.
why.microGeography: The parcel stands on the bank's east shoulder, 2.6 m above the water. The ground falls south to the sea.

playerPurpose.note: The second way down into the temple, where the loop comes out.

routes.why: The pilgrim track runs from Lilmoth to the north. It runs down the bank to the water opposite the gap in the teeth.
A spur leaves the track and crosses the bank. The spur ends at the west scaffold's door into the temple.
A short spur leaves the track for the east scaffold. The band keeps its watch at the east scaffold.

landmarks.notes: Six black teeth in a row in knee-deep water, each scrubbed white to the waterline.

occupants.cultureRole: The scrubber cleans the teeth down to the waterline.

approaches.sequence: The priests' track comes along the bank from the west. The track ends at the head of the pilgrim way. The way runs south between the two scaffolds to the water.
approaches.wayfinding: From the track's end the teeth show in a row out in the water. A stone door frame stands on the bank on each side of the way.

networkTerminals.why: The priests' track along the coast ends here. It ends at the head of the pilgrim way down to the water.

combatSpaces.why: In NI05 the splinter sect may turn on the Clutch here. The fight happens on the open bank between the two doors.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: catalogue record The Teeth of Sithis (sithis-temple, M1)
scaleGrounding.why: A priest, a scrubber and a small band keep the temple. The record names no keepers beyond these. The bank holds no houses.

candidates.why: The record sets the temple at the end of the pilgrim water. The bank meets the formation at that spot.
The next stretch of the same bank lies 45 m east. That stretch also falls to open water.
candidates.rejectedBecause: The plugin's two doors and the formation sit at the chosen spot. East of the chosen spot the bank has no teeth to frame.
